Iterated log-sum-exp smoothing with escalating sharpness and random tangent shakes optimized by L-BFGS, finished by trust-region LP polishing to tie near-contacts.
Shake the worst jammed points with adaptive Gaussian kicks and greedy tangential soft-max repulsion to hop basins, then squeeze with trust-region LP.
Shake the worst-contact cluster and re-insert the worst point, anneal a softmax of all cosines with L-BFGS, then re-balance with a trust-region LP that keeps all quasi-contacts.
Annealed LogSumExp Adam smoothing with random kicks and worst-point reinsertion to change basins, finished by trust-region LP equalization.
Shave the single isolated peak then globally re-optimize with annealed exponential-weighted repulsion and basin-hopping plus final trust-region LP polish.
Basin-hopping with annealed softmax repulsion optimized by Adam on the sphere plus short trust-region LP refinements and targeted kicks/resampling of worst-pair points.
Worst-point focused basin hopping with hole-reseeding under escalating log-sum-exp L-BFGS plus micro trust-region LP to tie the degenerate near-contact plateau.

Break the jammed core (53 points carry ~1000 ties while 166 rattle) with worst-subset kicks, opposite pair-breaks, cluster-expansion and farthest-hole reseeding followed by escalating log-sum-exp L-BFGS and greedy true-max micro moves.
Basin-hop the jammed contact core by kicking worst points and re-inserting rattlers at far voids, then squeeze with soft-max relaxation, L-BFGS sharpening and LP polishing.
Isolated-peak shaving plus focused basin-hopping that repeatedly kicks the worst pair and its crowded neighbours and re-anneals with sharpening soft-max repulsion before trust-region LP squeeze.

Alternate targeted basin hops (worst-point Gaussian kicks and greedy void re-insertion of jammed points) screened by soft-max tangential repulsion with short trust-region LP squeezes and a long final LP polish.
Break the single-pair bottleneck with worst-point Gaussian kicks, large-hole re-insertion and annealed soft-max tangential repulsion, squeezed by trust-region LP.
Trust-region linear programming with line-search to squeeze the single active contact and its 1e-8 plateau, alternated with targeted tangent kicks to the jammed points to change basin topology.

Wandering basin-hopping from the jammed core using worst-subset kicks, pair-breaks, cluster-expansion and farthest-hole reseeding with two-stage log-sum-exp L-BFGS and sideways moves plus high-beta sharpening and trust-region LP tying.
Jammed-core annealing with wandering basin-hops, collective cluster moves and void re-insertion followed by escalating soft-max L-BFGS and final trust-region LP squeeze.

Jammed isostatic core with zero rattlers needs subset surgery — kick worst clusters, reinsert at far voids and re-optimise only the moving subset with annealed soft-max L-BFGS before global squeeze and LP polish.
Rattler-recycled contact surgery that ejects jammed high-contact points into largest empty voids and re-relaxes with dual-temperature soft-max repulsion plus trust-region LP squeezes.

Metropolis basin-hopping from a wandering current state with worst-point kicks, jammed-cluster kicks and void re-insertion screened by annealed soft-max repulsion plus L-BFGS sharpening and short trust-region LP squeezes.

Shatter the jammed contact core by kill-and-fill void re-insertion of worst and highly-contacted clusters plus noisy tangential annealing, screened by soft-max repulsion and sharpened by L-BFGS and trust-region LP.
Wandering basin-hopping from the jammed core with clustered neighbourhood shakes and far-void re-insertions screened by noisy soft-max Langevin, sharpened by L-BFGS and trust-region LP.
Wandering subset-surgery basin-hopping with annealed soft-max L-BFGS plus tangent-space LP trust-region tying to squeeze the jammed core.
Target the single isolated maximal pair with void re-insertion and cluster surgery, then re-optimize with escalating soft-max L-BFGS and trust-region LP squeeze.

Wandering basin-hopping with jammed-manifold LP sideways slides plus worst-point hole reseeding, cluster pair-breaks and rattler moves screened by fast soft-max descent and two-stage L-BFGS with final trust-region LP tie-down.
Shatter the single-pair bottleneck by alternating isolated-peak shaving with void re-insertion of worst points and annealed soft-max repulsion plus L-BFGS and trust-region LP polish.

Jammed isostatic core with one rattler needs contact-topology rewiring — wandering basin-hops with worst-cluster kicks, collective shifts, pair-break repulsion and void reinsertion followed by two-stage soft-max L-BFGS and final trust-region LP squeeze.

Wandering Metropolis basin-hopping from a current state with jammed-cluster kicks and void kill-and-fill, screened by momentum soft-max repulsion and sharpened by alternating L-BFGS log-sum-exp and trust-region LP.

Rebuild the contact graph via N-homotopy: prune 19 worst points to 200, rejamming freely, then sequential maximin void re-insertion with annealed soft-max relaxation, plus the reverse overfilled 228-point jamming and pruning path.
direction: Use $N$-homotopy through easier and harder spherical codes: create a 200-point code by deleting the 19 points with largest per-point maximum (including the rattler where appropriate), optimise it freely until jammed, then add points back one at a time at maximin void candidates, with an annealed $\beta$ soft-max global re-optimisation and LP polish after every addition, so the contact graph is rebuilt sequentially on the way to 219; in parallel or in alternating trials do the reverse by optimising an overfilled 225–230-point code and pruning its worst points back to 219, because traversing neighbouring $N$ values can enter a 219-point basin inaccessible by perturbing the current jammed configuration.

idea: Wandering basin-hopping from the jammed core with uphill Metropolis acceptance, mass cluster kicks and multi-point far-void reinsertion, screened by soft-max repulsion and sharpened by L-BFGS with final LP squeeze.

Break the isostatically jammed 218+1 core with topology-changing moves — block resampling, greedy void re-insertion, and coherent cap rotations — screened by annealed soft-max L-BFGS and finished with high-beta sharpening plus trust-region LP.
Impose three finite orthogonal symmetries to force different basins then release to full optimisation.
direction: Search a symmetry-constrained basin that local optimisation cannot reach: choose a finite orthogonal group such as the order-12 dihedral group generated by a cyclic permutation of the six coordinates and a coordinate reversal, represent 216 of the points as 18 full group orbits plus 3 additional free or specially constrained points, optimise only the orbit representatives with an annealed log-sum-exp L-BFGS objective (computing gradients by summing over the 12 transformed copies), then gradually release the symmetry by using the symmetric optimum as an initialisation for unrestricted soft-max optimisation and LP polishing; repeat for two or three groups (for example signed flips of three coordinates with orbit size 8, or a 6-cycle alone) and keep the best released result, since even an imperfect symmetric seed can place the code in a different contact topology.

Topology-shattering basin hopping with void kill-fill, cluster shatters and heavy-tail kicks screened by soft-max relaxation and sharpened by two-stage L-BFGS plus trust-region LP squeeze.

Escape the jammed 1080-contact vertex by kill-and-fill void re-insertion that removes overloaded max-pair points and greedily reinserts them into the largest holes to force the rattler into the stress network, screened by soft-max L-BFGS and trust-region LP.

Escape the isostatically jammed basin with large destroy-and-repair basin-hopping using full random reinsertion and large collective shakes followed by multi-beta soft-max L-BFGS and trust-region LP squeeze.
Large delete-and-rebuild surgery that removes rattlers plus dense contact clusters, relaxes the core, then greedily reinserts points from 50k samples with local refinement.
direction: Perform large-scale delete-and-rebuild surgery rather than kicking one to three points: starting from `best.npy`, identify the rattler plus points in the densest/highest-degree contact clusters, delete a random or clustered block of 12–24 points (breaking hundreds of contacts), LP/soft-max re-optimise the remaining 195–207 points until they jam at a lower cosine, then reinsert the deleted points one at a time by sampling about 50,000 random sphere candidates, refining the best few by minimising their maximum dot product with the current set, and after each insertion running L-BFGS only on the inserted point and its 20 nearest neighbours followed by a short global LP polish; repeat with different deleted blocks for about 120 seconds, keep only insertions whose fully polished score beats the incumbent, and always retain the incumbent as fallback.

idea: Dual-stress-guided rewiring that caps hub and weakly-stressed contacts below max-delta during high-beta soft-max re-jamming then LP re-polishes to force a new contact topology with integrated rattler.
direction: Dual-stress-guided contact rewiring: After an LP polish, extract the LP dual weights (or solve the non-negative least-squares force-balance problem) for the $\sim1{,}080$ active contacts and identify redundant or weakly stressed contacts, contacts incident to the highest-degree hubs (degree $14$--$15$), and small clusters whose removal creates a low-dimensional mechanism. For many trials, choose one hub or one $6$--$15$-edge cluster, add hard caps or a strong penalty keeping those chosen pairs below $\mathrm{max}-0.001$ to $\mathrm{max}-0.003$ during a high-$\beta$ soft-max re-jam, then remove the caps, re-polish with the LP, and record the new contact graph. Keep a diverse pool ranked first by score and second by contact-graph Jaccard distance from the incumbent, specifically rewarding outcomes where a former hub drops below degree $\sim10$ and the rattler gains contacts, rather than repeatedly returning to the identical graph.

idea: Finite-temperature parallel tempering over log-sum-exp smoothed energies with projected Adam-Langevin dynamics and Metropolis swaps plus periodic copy-only quenches.
direction: Run genuine finite-temperature parallel tempering on a smooth potential instead of greedy basin hopping: maintain 6–8 replicas of the full configuration at different log-sum-exp inverse temperatures (for example $\beta$ geometrically spaced from about 50 to 3000) or equivalent Riesz energies, evolve each by projected tangent Langevin/Adam steps with noise scaled to its temperature, periodically attempt replica swaps with the usual Metropolis criterion on the smooth energy, and every few seconds quench a copy of the coldest replica with LP polish only to record a candidate score while leaving the tempering replicas unquenched; this allows coordinated uphill moves in which many contacts temporarily worsen and the topology can rewire, with the best quenched configuration (or the loaded incumbent if none improves) returned before the time limit.

idea: Rattler-first void-expansion homotopy that freezes the zero-contact point, forces its neighbours delta below the core max with masked soft-max L-BFGS, alternates with maximin void re-insertion and release-plus-polish.
direction: Rattler-first void-expansion homotopy: Identify the zero-contact rattler $r$ and freeze it, then re-optimise the other $218$ points not merely to minimise the usual max-cosine but to minimise it subject to forcing $r$ to become active, e.g. LP/soft-max steps with the extra target $\langle x_r,x_i\rangle \le t-\delta$ initially for its $8$--$12$ nearest neighbours, sweeping $\delta=10^{-5},2\times10^{-5},5\times10^{-5},10^{-4}$ and releasing $r$ after each step. Alternate this with moving $r$ to the refined largest void of the current core (search $20{,}000$ random candidates plus local void refinement) and then re-running the forced-activation optimisation, accepting only configurations in which $r$ ends with $\ge5$ contacts within $10^{-7}$ of the final max and the $218$-core max has dropped. Finish each accepted topology with the standard trust-region LP polish and always keep the incumbent as fallback.

idea: Sample diverse low-order signed-permutation subgroups preserving a 4+2 coordinate split, optimize only orbit representatives plus a small free tail under the soft-max objective with exact group replication, then release the best symmetric codes with tangent noise to free L-BFGS and LP polish.
direction: Large-symmetry orbit construction from scratch: Go far beyond the previously tried order-$6$/$8$/$12$ groups by enumerating signed-permutation subgroups of order $48$, $96$, and $192$ (coordinate permutations combined with even sign flips and coordinate-pair sign blocks), generating orbits of sizes such as $48+48+48+48+24+3=219$, $96+96+24+3=219$, or $48+48+48+48+12+12+3=219$, and optimising only the few orbit representatives under the soft-max objective with exact group replication. Randomly sample many subgroups/conjugates and representative initialisations, score the fully symmetric codes, then break the symmetry gradually by adding tangent noise of sizes $10^{-4},10^{-3},10^{-2}$ to individual points and releasing to free L-BFGS plus LP polish. This searches low-dimensional, highly structured basins that cannot be reached by perturbing the disordered incumbent, while the final release allows the symmetry to survive only if it is actually beneficial.

idea: Build the full half-integer lattice universe in R6, greedily select 219 directions minimizing max cosine then count, improve by maximin void swaps, relax with soft-max L-BFGS and orbit-constrained dihedral optimization before LP polish.
direction: Search from scratch in an algebraic/lattice candidate universe for the missing symmetric structure. Generate all signed permutations of patterns such as $(1,1,0,0,0,0)/\sqrt2$, $(1,1,1,1,0,0)/2$, $(1,1,1,0,0,0)/\sqrt3$, $(1,\tfrac12,\tfrac12,\tfrac12,\tfrac12,0)$ normalised, and $E_6/D_6$-style half-integer vectors with coordinates in $\{0,\pm\tfrac12,\pm1\}$ normalised, deduplicate them, and greedily select 219 points minimising first the maximum cosine and second the number of pairs attaining it, followed by pairwise-swap local search on the candidate pool. Then relax the selected set with soft-max L-BFGS ($\beta=50\to500\to5000$) and LP polish; in parallel, try an orbit-constrained stage under a signed-permutation/dihedral group generated from 12–36 representatives before releasing symmetry. Compare against, but do not initialise from, the incumbent except as a guaranteed fallback output.

idea: Rattler-integrating basin hopping that transplants the free point plus overloaded hubs into fresh voids and re-jams rattler-centred neighbourhoods with frozen-core L-BFGS before global soft-max/LP polishing to force a new contact topology.

Sample 4+2 product subgroups of B6 of orders 48/96/192 with random conjugates, optimise few orbit representatives plus free remainder under exact group replication with soft-max L-BFGS, then break symmetry with tangent noise and release to free L-BFGS plus trust-region LP polish alongside incumbent polishing.

idea: Egalitarian per-point softmax with LP-dual stress reweighting and annealing to balance contacts and integrate the rattler into a new basin.
direction: Replace the purely global max objective by an egalitarian per-point minimax/stress-reweighting optimisation. Extract LP dual stresses for contacts within $10^{-6}$ of the maximum, identify zero-stress contacts, high-stress hubs, and the rattler, then minimise $\sum_i \mathrm{softmax}_{\beta}( \{\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\}_j )$ — a soft maximum per point summed over points — with pair weights $w_{ij}= \epsilon+\text{dual stress}_{ij}$ for near-contacts, annealing $\beta=100\to3000$, so that overloaded points are pushed down and the rattler is forced to acquire useful near-contacts instead of being ignored by the global max. Alternate 200–500 L-BFGS steps of this objective with short LP polishes, periodically recomputing stresses and dropping persistently zero-stress active pairs from the weighted set while adding pairs entering slack $<10^{-4}$. The intended endpoint is a different, fully stressed basin with no rattler and minimum contact degree at least 6; keep the best exact configuration encountered and fall back to the incumbent if none beats it.

idea: Kill-and-fill void reinsertion with greedy hole sampling plus local void refinement and soft-max L-BFGS basin hopping to change contact topology and escape the isostatic jam.

idea: Second-order nullspace escape from the isostatic LP vertex via sparse Jacobian SVD modes with exact spherical retraction and selective LP re-polish.
direction: Implement a second-order nullspace escape from the incumbent. Build tangent bases $B_i\in\mathbb R^{6\times5}$ with $B_i^\top x_i=0$, form the sparse Jacobian $A$ of all pairs with cosine above $\mathrm{maxcos}-10^{-6}$ in the $219\cdot5$ tangent coordinates (fix the 15 rotational modes and initially freeze the rattler), and compute the 20–40 smallest singular vectors of $A$ with `scipy.sparse.linalg.svds`. For each mode and each sign, retract trial steps $x_i\leftarrow \mathrm{normalize}(x_i+\epsilon B_i v_i)$ for $\epsilon\in\{0.003,0.01,0.03\}$ (both sphere-exact, not linearised), rank trials by the resulting number of pairs above $\mathrm{maxcos}-10^{-7}$ and by exact max cosine, then run the existing LP polish only on the best few trials. Accept only an exact improvement; otherwise retain the incumbent as fallback. This directly searches curved feasible directions that the linearised LP declares blocked.

idea: Block-transplant basin hopping that removes rattlers, worst and overloaded-hub points into maximin voids with large kicks then re-jams with two-stage soft-max L-BFGS and selective LP polishing.
Delete the rattler plus a high-degree hub and their shared closest neighbours and greedily reinsert maximin replacements from 20k candidates with refinement, then rejamming in expanding shells.
direction: Do contact-topology surgery by deleting and reinserting a small cluster rather than perturbing all points. In each trial delete 3–5 points chosen from specific roles — the rattler, one degree-$\ge14$ hub, and 1–3 of their shared/high-cosine neighbours — generate at least 20,000 random unit candidates plus local refinements of the best candidates against the frozen survivors, and greedily insert replacements maximising the minimum angle first to survivors and then to previously inserted points. Optimise only the inserted points and survivors with cosine $>0.55$ to any inserted point using soft-max L-BFGS ($\beta=200\to2000$), then release neighbours in expanding shells, finish with LP polish, and repeat with different role-based deletions/seeds inside the time budget. Success should be judged after full release by exact max cosine and by whether the active-pair count/set has changed, not by the frozen-stage objective; always return the incumbent if no trial improves it.
